A syntactically malformed Rego file fails regal with potentially misleading diagnostics before the root formatting error is surfaced.","evidence":"policy-check.yml:339-351 step 'Lint policies with Regal' precedes policy-check.yml:353-361 step 'Check policy formatting with OPA'. policies/README.md:60 step 6 specifies: 'Run `find policies -type f -name '*.rego' -print0 | xargs -0 opa fmt --fail`' first, then 'regal lint'. Contributor following README runs checks in reverse order from CI, sees different failure messages, and may fix a regal diagnostic that would have been a formatting error had they run opa fmt first.","impact":"Creates friction in the contribute-a-rule workflow; a malformed but regal-passing rule submitted without local opa fmt verification passes the README checklist check but fails CI on the formatting step. Low blast radius but undermines the self-service reliability of the contributing guide.","mitigation":"Swap policy-check.yml steps so 'Check policy formatting with OPA' (opa fmt --fail) runs before 'Lint policies with Regal', matching the README sequence.","lens":"safety"},{"id":"R2-SAF-MIN-03","severity":"MIN","status":"open","carry_forward":true,"r1_id":"SAFETY-007","claim":"SCP-R-003 JSON boolean attestation regex `(?s).*\"scp:vendoring-attested\"\\s*:\\s*true.*` matches 'truenotreally' as a substring, allowing a malformed boolean value to pass the attestation check.","evidence":"SCP-R-003.rego:43-44 scp_r_003_has_attestation_marker second clause: `regex.match(`(?s).*\"scp:vendoring-attested\"\\s*:\\s*true.*`, content)`. The pattern requires the literal string 'true' followed by `.*`; 'truenotreally' matches because 'true' is a prefix of the word and `.*` consumes the remainder. Rego operates on raw string content, not parsed JSON; no word boundary or non-word-character anchor terminates 'true'. A package.json containing `{\"scp:vendoring-attested\": truenotreally}` (syntactically invalid JSON but plausible raw string) passes the marker check.","impact":"A careless or adversarial developer can commit a package.json with a non-boolean value for scp:vendoring-attested and bypass SCP-R-003 attestation validation. While a JSON-aware tool would reject the file, the Rego rule cannot distinguish.","mitigation":"Tighten the regex to require a non-word character or end-of-input after 'true': `(?s).*\"scp:vendoring-attested\"\\s*:\\s*true[^a-zA-Z0-9_].*` or use the \\b word boundary anchor if supported by OPA's re2 engine. But the fixture tree that the workflow selftest harness uses for conftest evaluation has no deny fixture exercising services.<name>.auth.mode = mode.invalid.","impact":"If scp_r_001_mode_records second definition is accidentally removed or its condition changed, OPA tests catch the regression. Modifying either without CODEOWNERS protection allows silent weakening of the gate without the governance review layer that protects the Rego rules.","mitigation":"Add to CODEOWNERS: `schemas/** @jrnb2024` and `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml @jrnb2024`. Per WP-SCP-020 §4 slice 020K, @jrnb2024 is the only maintainer; the same owner applies.","lens":"safety"},{"id":"R2-SAF-MIN-06","severity":"MIN","status":"open","carry_forward":false,"r1_id":"F-COR-006","claim":"SCP-R-001 silently passes when auth_contract is present but accepted_modes is explicitly null, absent, or a non-array scalar. No deny is emitted for this structurally invalid shape.","evidence":"SCP-R-001.rego:110-112: `accepted_modes := object.get(auth_contract, \"accepted_modes\", null); is_array(accepted_modes); some index, entry in accepted_modes`. If accepted_modes is null or a non-array, is_array evaluates FALSE, no scp_r_001_mode_records entry is generated, and all four deny rules (which iterate over scp_r_001_mode_records) produce 0 findings. Input `{services:{svc:{prod:{runtime_contract:{auth_contract:{accepted_modes:null}}}}}}` → 0 denies. No test covers this path. The flat auth second definition (SCP-R-001.rego:115-125) also silently passes when the auth object is present but its mode field is null.","impact":"A developer or adversary can set `accepted_modes: null` in services.yml to suppress all SCP-R-001 auth-mode validation for that service without producing any deny finding. Trains reviewers to ignore red CI annotations, degrading the signal value of genuine SCP-E003 deny annotations.","evidence":"policy-check.yml:557 `print(f\"::error file={config_path},title=SCP-E006::{rule_id} disabled: {reason}; expires_at={expires_at}\")`. The SCP-E006 record appended at policy-check.yml:401-423 has reason='no-manifest-applicable' and is not a failure condition. AC3 in the dispatch package describes SCP-E006 as an observability record. ::error renders as a red annotation in GitHub PR UI. Every PR on a repo with no manifest files in its diff will show a persistent ::error annotation for SCP-E006, normalising red annotations as informational.","impact":"Reviewers learn to ignore ::error annotations from scp/policy-check. When a genuine SCP-E003 deny fires, the annotation is in the same 'red noise' bucket and may be overlooked. Degrades the human-facing signal of the enforcement gate.","mitigation":"Change the SCP-E006 emission at policy-check.yml:557 from `::error` to `::notice`. No deny rules iterate over an empty input so the deny count would be 0, but the clause body expression `count(input) == 0` is never reached TRUE. OPA coverage tracks expression-level evaluation.","impact":"Potential AC-5 coverage shortfall for SCP-R-002 at the --threshold 90 gate; if OPA counts this clause as an uncovered expression the combined coverage of SCP-R-002.rego may fall below 90%, blocking CI.","mitigation":"Add test_scp_r_002_allows_empty_waiver_array with input_value := [] expecting count(scp_r_002_results(input_value)) == 0.","lens":"safety"},{"id":"R2-SAF-nit-02","severity":"nit","status":"open","carry_forward":false,"r1_id":null,"claim":"OPA coverage --threshold 90 at the per-rule enforcement step measures combined coverage across both the rule file and its test file; high test-file coverage (test function bodies are executed) can offset low rule-file branch coverage, making the gate softer than intended.","evidence":"policy-check.yml:385-392 runs `opa test \"${rule_file}\" \"${test_file}\" --coverage --threshold 90 --fail-on-empty -v`. OPA --coverage computes expression coverage across all loaded files. If scp_r_001_test.rego (7 test functions with 40+ expression lines all executed) contributes heavily to the numerator, a rule file with 80% expression coverage could produce a combined score above 90%. The step does not use per-file coverage breakdown or a rule-file-only coverage report.","impact":"The coverage gate may pass despite a rule file having below-90% expression coverage, leaving untested denial branches undetected. The gate is directionally correct but its threshold enforcement may be weaker than AC-5 intends for novel rules added by future contributors.","mitigation":"Parse the JSON coverage output (`opa test --coverage --format json`) and assert per-file coverage for the specific rule file exceeds 90%, rather than relying on the combined threshold. Alternatively, run `opa test --coverage --threshold 90` on the rule file alone without the test file to get rule-only coverage (if OPA supports loading test rules without a test file — if not, accept the combined approach and document the caveat in policies/README.md).","lens":"safety"}],"fixpoint_assessment":{"status":"NOT_REACHED","blocker":"R2-SAF-MAJ-01 — residual SCP-R-002 bypass via object arrays with no recognised key fields. scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload remains FALSE for [{\"unknown\":\"x\"}], causing all four deny blocks that guard on it to never fire. Fix is a single three-line clause addition to scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload plus a test and fixture. Must close before fixpoint is declared.","note":"Once R2-SAF-MAJ-01 is closed, the remaining seven MIN and two nit findings carry no active exploit path in the current CI enforcement route and §4.3 fixpoint criteria (APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS MIN/nit-only) would be satisfied."},"self_reported_concerns":["R2-SAF-MAJ-01 and the previously-open F-COR-008 (MIN, correctness) are the same root cause viewed from different lenses. The two-line fix is low-risk and should be bundled with a deny fixture to ensure fixture-driven coverage.","The OPA coverage enforcement step (policy-check.yml:363-392) is structurally correct and closes CG-001 cleanly. The deny fixture at testdata/SCP-R-002/deny/waivers.json now correctly produces a deny because it omits reason, and the allow fixture at testdata/SCP-R-002/allow/waivers.json now correctly allows because it includes reason. The schema chain (waiver.schema.json, waivers-file.schema.json, scp_r_002_required_keys, fixtures) is self-consistent."]}

findings.claim: Residual SCP-R-002 bypass: an array of objects with no recognised key fields (e.g. [{}] or [{"custom_key":"x"}]) passes all five deny rules with zero violations, silently evading waiver integrity validation.
findings.evidence: SCP-R-002.rego:18-28 first deny fires only when `not is_object(entry)`; {} is an object so this branch does not fire. SCP-R-002.rego:89-100 scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload clause 2 requires `some key in {"approved_by","created_at","expires_at","rule_id","finding_id","waiver_id","reason"}; object.get(entry, key, null) != null`; {} satisfies none, so scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload is FALSE. SCP-R-002.rego:30-87 deny rules 2-5 all begin with `scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload` → do not fire. Net result: input [{"unrecognised":"payload"}] → 0 denies. The fr1 fix removed the scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload guard from deny rule 1 (closing the scalar-string variant of SAFETY-001) but did not add a third clause `scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload if { is_array(input); count(input) > 0 }` to cover all non-empty arrays, as recommended in F-COR-008 mitigation. No test covers this path; scp_r_002_test.rego tests 4 and 5 only exercise non-object scalars and mixed-object-plus-scalar arrays respectively.
findings.impact: An adversary or misconfigured automation can commit waivers.json as [{}] to bypass all SCP-R-002 integrity checks. In 020C scope the bypass allows structurally invalid waivers to pass silently without flagging, corrupting the governance audit trail. In 020C.1 scope the unrecognised-key object cannot match any rule_id or finding_id so it cannot suppress a specific violation, but the Rego integrity gate is semantically circumvented; a future rule change that reads unguarded data.waivers could be surprised. The waivers-file.schema.json bypass gate (policy-check.yml:496) would reject [{}] via additionalProperties:false, but only when scp_bypass=true; for normal workflow runs (scp_bypass=false) the Rego gate is the only check.
findings.mitigation: Add a third clause to scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload at SCP-R-002.rego after line 100: `scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload if { is_array(input); count(input) > 0 }`. This makes the second through fifth deny rules apply to all non-empty arrays, not just those already containing a recognisable waiver key. The existing is_object guard on deny rules 2-5 continues to correctly skip non-object entries (which are caught by deny rule 1). Add test_scp_r_002_denies_all_unrecognised_key_object with input [{"custom_key":"x"}] expecting at least 3 denies (approved_by, expires_at missing; reason missing; rule_id/finding_id missing). Also add policies/testdata/SCP-R-002/deny/waivers_unknown_key.json to ensure fixture-driven coverage.

findings.claim: Regal binary downloaded and executed without SHA256 pin or Sigstore attestation, unlike OPA (SHA256+Sigstore) and Conftest (SHA256+archive_sha256). A compromised Regal release binary could execute arbitrary code in the CI runner.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:224 `curl ... "${REGAL_REPO}/${REGAL_ASSET}" --output "${BIN_DIR}/regal"` — no SHA256 verification follows. policy-check.yml:226 `"${BIN_DIR}/regal" version` is a smoke-test, not integrity verification. REGAL_VERSION=0.40.0 hardcoded at line 144 not read from scripts/.tool-versions. scp-policy-check.lock contains no regal entry. OPA binary gets `gh attestation verify` at line 211; Conftest gets sha256 and archive_sha256 checked at lines 167-221. Regal gets neither.
findings.impact: A compromised Regal release binary or a MITM on the GitHub release download executes with full runner access to the checked-out repository, including policies/, schemas/, and any secrets present in the runner environment. Blast radius is highest-severity in the supply chain because regal runs before conftest and could tamper with policy files.
findings.mitigation: Add regal sha256 pins to scripts/scp-policy-check.lock for linux-x64 and linux-arm64. Move REGAL_VERSION to scripts/.tool-versions. Apply `verify_sha256 "${BIN_DIR}/regal" "${REGAL_SHA256}"` after download using the existing verify_sha256 function (defined at line 171). Consider adding Sigstore verification when regal publishes attestations.

findings.claim: CI executes regal lint (policy-check.yml:339) before opa fmt --fail (policy-check.yml:353), inverting the developer checklist order in policies/README.md step 6. A syntactically malformed Rego file fails regal with potentially misleading diagnostics before the root formatting error is surfaced.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:339-351 step 'Lint policies with Regal' precedes policy-check.yml:353-361 step 'Check policy formatting with OPA'. policies/README.md:60 step 6 specifies: 'Run `find policies -type f -name '*.rego' -print0 | xargs -0 opa fmt --fail`' first, then 'regal lint'. Contributor following README runs checks in reverse order from CI, sees different failure messages, and may fix a regal diagnostic that would have been a formatting error had they run opa fmt first.
findings.impact: Creates friction in the contribute-a-rule workflow; a malformed but regal-passing rule submitted without local opa fmt verification passes the README checklist check but fails CI on the formatting step. Low blast radius but undermines the self-service reliability of the contributing guide.
findings.mitigation: Swap policy-check.yml steps so 'Check policy formatting with OPA' (opa fmt --fail) runs before 'Lint policies with Regal', matching the README sequence.

findings.claim: SCP-R-003 JSON boolean attestation regex `(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true.*` matches 'truenotreally' as a substring, allowing a malformed boolean value to pass the attestation check.
findings.evidence: SCP-R-003.rego:43-44 scp_r_003_has_attestation_marker second clause: `regex.match(`(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true.*`, content)`. The pattern requires the literal string 'true' followed by `.*`; 'truenotreally' matches because 'true' is a prefix of the word and `.*` consumes the remainder. Rego operates on raw string content, not parsed JSON; no word boundary or non-word-character anchor terminates 'true'. A package.json containing `{"scp:vendoring-attested": truenotreally}` (syntactically invalid JSON but plausible raw string) passes the marker check.
findings.impact: A careless or adversarial developer can commit a package.json with a non-boolean value for scp:vendoring-attested and bypass SCP-R-003 attestation validation. While a JSON-aware tool would reject the file, the Rego rule cannot distinguish.
findings.mitigation: Tighten the regex to require a non-word character or end-of-input after 'true': `(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true[^a-zA-Z0-9_].*` or use the \b word boundary anchor if supported by OPA's re2 engine. Add a deny test case with content 'truenotreally' and verify it fires.

findings.claim: SCP-R-001 flat auth deny path has OPA test coverage (added in fr1) but has no testdata fixture. A regression in scp_r_001_mode_records flat-auth definition would not be caught by fixture-driven conftest evaluation.
findings.evidence: policies/testdata/SCP-R-001/deny/ contains only services.yml (runtime_contract nested path; deny/services.yml:1-9). No deny/flat_auth/services.yml or equivalent. scp_r_001_test.rego:57-63 (test_scp_r_001_denies_flat_auth_unknown_mode) and :65-74 (test_scp_r_001_denies_flat_auth_bearer_legacy_invalid_date) add OPA unit tests for the flat auth deny path (scp_r_001_mode_records second definition at SCP-R-001.rego:115-125), closing the R1 F-COR-003 test gap. But the fixture tree that the workflow selftest harness uses for conftest evaluation has no deny fixture exercising services.<name>.auth.mode = mode.invalid.
findings.impact: If scp_r_001_mode_records second definition is accidentally removed or its condition changed, OPA tests catch the regression. But the fixture-driven conftest path (workflow-selftest.yml) never exercises the flat auth deny, so an integration regression in that path would not surface via the selftest harness.
findings.mitigation:
Add policies/testdata/SCP-R-001/deny/flat_auth/services.yml with content: `services:
  api:
    auth:
      mode: mode.invalid` and verify it produces a deny finding when run through conftest against the rule bundle.

findings.claim: CODEOWNERS covers only policies/** leaving schemas/waiver.schema.json, schemas/waivers-file.schema.json, and .github/workflows/policy-check.yml unprotected. A PR weakening the waiver schema required fields or removing threshold enforcement in the workflow has no designated-reviewer gate.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS:1 `policies/** @jrnb2024` — the only entry. A PR that removes `reason` from schemas/waivers-file.schema.json required array, or deletes the `if effective_denies and SCP_THRESHOLD == 'deny': sys.exit(1)` block at policy-check.yml:598-600, or reduces the bypass gate's schema validation at policy-check.yml:487-511, bypasses the CODEOWNERS review gate that protects the Rego rules themselves.
findings.impact: The integrity of the entire policy enforcement pipeline depends equally on schema contracts and the workflow enforcement logic. Modifying either without CODEOWNERS protection allows silent weakening of the gate without the governance review layer that protects the Rego rules.
findings.mitigation: Add to CODEOWNERS: `schemas/** @jrnb2024` and `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml @jrnb2024`. Per WP-SCP-020 §4 slice 020K, @jrnb2024 is the only maintainer; the same owner applies.

findings.claim: SCP-R-001 silently passes when auth_contract is present but accepted_modes is explicitly null, absent, or a non-array scalar. No deny is emitted for this structurally invalid shape.
findings.evidence: SCP-R-001.rego:110-112: `accepted_modes := object.get(auth_contract, "accepted_modes", null); is_array(accepted_modes); some index, entry in accepted_modes`. If accepted_modes is null or a non-array, is_array evaluates FALSE, no scp_r_001_mode_records entry is generated, and all four deny rules (which iterate over scp_r_001_mode_records) produce 0 findings. Input `{services:{svc:{prod:{runtime_contract:{auth_contract:{accepted_modes:null}}}}}}` → 0 denies. No test covers this path. The flat auth second definition (SCP-R-001.rego:115-125) also silently passes when the auth object is present but its mode field is null.
findings.impact: A developer or adversary can set `accepted_modes: null` in services.yml to suppress all SCP-R-001 auth-mode validation for that service without producing any deny finding. The rule provides no deny signal when the auth contract structure exists but accepted_modes is deliberately nulled.
findings.mitigation: Add a deny branch: when auth_contract is an object and accepted_modes is missing, null, or not an array, emit `deny contains {"message": sprintf("%s.auth_contract.accepted_modes must be a non-empty array of mode objects", [path]), ...}`. Add a test and fixture exercising accepted_modes: null.

findings.claim: SCP-E006 no-manifest-applicable observability record is emitted as ::error annotation (policy-check.yml:557), semantically incorrect for a non-blocking informational signal. Trains reviewers to ignore red CI annotations, degrading the signal value of genuine SCP-E003 deny annotations.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:557 `print(f"::error file={config_path},title=SCP-E006::{rule_id} disabled: {reason}; expires_at={expires_at}")`. The SCP-E006 record appended at policy-check.yml:401-423 has reason='no-manifest-applicable' and is not a failure condition. AC3 in the dispatch package describes SCP-E006 as an observability record. ::error renders as a red annotation in GitHub PR UI. Every PR on a repo with no manifest files in its diff will show a persistent ::error annotation for SCP-E006, normalising red annotations as informational.
findings.impact: Reviewers learn to ignore ::error annotations from scp/policy-check. When a genuine SCP-E003 deny fires, the annotation is in the same 'red noise' bucket and may be overlooked. Degrades the human-facing signal of the enforcement gate.
findings.mitigation: Change the SCP-E006 emission at policy-check.yml:557 from `::error` to `::notice`. Only emit ::error for entries with a reason indicating an active disable (not no-manifest-applicable).

findings.claim: scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload empty-array clause (SCP-R-002.rego:89-92) is never exercised TRUE in any test; OPA expression coverage penalises this uncovered branch, risking sub-90% coverage on the --threshold 90 gate.
findings.evidence: scp_r_002_test.rego contains no test passing input_value := []. The six tests use arrays of length 1 or 2. SCP-R-002.rego:89-92 `scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload if { is_array(input); count(input) == 0 }` requires an empty array to evaluate the clause TRUE. No deny rules iterate over an empty input so the deny count would be 0, but the clause body expression `count(input) == 0` is never reached TRUE. OPA coverage tracks expression-level evaluation.
findings.impact: Potential AC-5 coverage shortfall for SCP-R-002 at the --threshold 90 gate; if OPA counts this clause as an uncovered expression the combined coverage of SCP-R-002.rego may fall below 90%, blocking CI.
findings.mitigation: Add test_scp_r_002_allows_empty_waiver_array with input_value := [] expecting count(scp_r_002_results(input_value)) == 0.

findings.claim: OPA coverage --threshold 90 at the per-rule enforcement step measures combined coverage across both the rule file and its test file; high test-file coverage (test function bodies are executed) can offset low rule-file branch coverage, making the gate softer than intended.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:385-392 runs `opa test "${rule_file}" "${test_file}" --coverage --threshold 90 --fail-on-empty -v`. OPA --coverage computes expression coverage across all loaded files. If scp_r_001_test.rego (7 test functions with 40+ expression lines all executed) contributes heavily to the numerator, a rule file with 80% expression coverage could produce a combined score above 90%. The step does not use per-file coverage breakdown or a rule-file-only coverage report.
findings.impact: The coverage gate may pass despite a rule file having below-90% expression coverage, leaving untested denial branches undetected. The gate is directionally correct but its threshold enforcement may be weaker than AC-5 intends for novel rules added by future contributors.
findings.mitigation: Parse the JSON coverage output (`opa test --coverage --format json`) and assert per-file coverage for the specific rule file exceeds 90%, rather than relying on the combined threshold. Alternatively, run `opa test --coverage --threshold 90` on the rule file alone without the test file to get rule-only coverage (if OPA supports loading test rules without a test file — if not, accept the combined approach and document the caveat in policies/README.md).

fixpoint_assessment.blocker: R2-SAF-MAJ-01 — residual SCP-R-002 bypass via object arrays with no recognised key fields. scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload remains FALSE for [{"unknown":"x"}], causing all four deny blocks that guard on it to never fire. Fix is a single three-line clause addition to scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload plus a test and fixture. Must close before fixpoint is declared.
fixpoint_assessment.note: Once R2-SAF-MAJ-01 is closed, the remaining seven MIN and two nit findings carry no active exploit path in the current CI enforcement route and §4.3 fixpoint criteria (APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS MIN/nit-only) would be satisfied.

r1_closure_verification.evidence: policy-check.yml:363-392 adds step 'Enforce per-rule OPA coverage' which iterates over every policies/SCP-R-*.rego, derives the matching test file via tr '[:upper:]-' '[:lower:]_', and runs `opa test "${rule_file}" "${test_file}" --coverage --threshold 90 --fail-on-empty -v` under set -euo pipefail. Exits 1 with SCP-E001 when the test file is missing. The per-rule threshold gate now blocks merge on coverage drop below 90%.

SCP-R-002.rego:18-28 first deny block no longer carries a scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload guard; it fires for any array element satisfying not is_object(entry). Input ["not-a-waiver"] now produces 1 deny (confirmed by test_scp_r_002_denies_scalar_only_arrays:49-55 expecting count 1). However, input [{}] is an object (not is_object({}) = FALSE) so the first deny does not fire; scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload (lines 89-100) is FALSE for {} because it has no recognised keys; all four remaining deny rules (lines 30-87) require scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload → do not fire → 0 denies. The object-with-no-recognised-keys bypass variant identified in F-COR-008 (correctness/MIN) is unaddressed and escalates to the primary open safety bypass. See R2-SAF-MAJ-01.

schemas/waivers-file.schema.json confirmed present in repo (Glob result). self_reported_concerns: R2-SAF-MAJ-01 and the previously-open F-COR-008 (MIN, correctness) are the same root cause viewed from different lenses. The fr1 mitigation for SAFETY-001 correctly removed the guard from the non-object-entry deny rule but did not implement the broader fix (unconditional non-empty array detection) recommended in F-COR-008. The two-line fix is low-risk and should be bundled with a deny fixture to ensure fixture-driven coverage.

The OPA coverage enforcement step (policy-check.yml:363-392) is structurally correct and closes CG-001 cleanly. The nit about combined rule+test file coverage (R2-SAF-nit-02) does not constitute a gate bypass since test files are short and the denominator is dominated by rule expressions at the current scale of 3 rules; it becomes a concern only when rules grow substantially larger than their test files.

SAFETY-003 (reason field) is correctly closed. The deny fixture at testdata/SCP-R-002/deny/waivers.json now correctly produces a deny because it omits reason, and the allow fixture at testdata/SCP-R-002/allow/waivers.json now correctly allows because it includes reason. structured_review.summary: The fr1 wave closes the CRIT and 4 of 5 safety MAJs and all correctness MAJs. The one outstanding MAJ is a residual bypass in SCP-R-002: an object array with no recognised key fields (e.g. [{}]) passes the waiver validation gate entirely because scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload evaluates to false and only the first deny rule — which guards on not is_object — can fire, but objects satisfy is_object. Fix is a one-line third clause to scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload. Seven MIN and two nit carry without change from R1.
structured_review.verdict_rationale: fr1 correctly closes the sole CRIT (CG-001 coverage gate now enforced in CI at policy-check.yml:363-392) and four of the five safety MAJ findings (SAFETY-002: waivers-file.schema.json created; SAFETY-003: reason added to scp_r_002_required_keys; SAFETY-004: past-date and futurity validation implemented in both SCP-R-001 and SCP-R-002; SAFETY-001 scalar-entry variant: first deny rule guard removed, scalar arrays now caught). However, SAFETY-001 is only partially closed: the scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload heuristic (SCP-R-002.rego:89-100) still yields FALSE for arrays whose entries are objects with no recognised key, allowing [{}] or [{"unknown":"x"}] to pass all five deny rules with zero violations (new finding R2-SAF-MAJ-01). One MAJ is open. Seven MIN and two nit carry forward. Fixpoint criterion §4.3 (APPROVED or APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS-MIN/nit-only) is not satisfied.
